column1: 2015-09-14T00:00:00Z;14-september-2015-chikungunya-en;;;Chikungunya – Senegal;Chikungunya is a viral disease transmitted to humans by infected mosquitoes. It causes fever and severe joint pain. Other symptoms include muscle pain

column6: Asia
column7: Latin America and the Indian subcontinent. Senegal was affected by the disease in 2009.;;On 9 September 2015

column2: UNICEF
column3: the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
column4: and Médecins sans Frontières (MSF). It works closely with vaccine manufacturers. It was established in 1997 following exceptionally large and deadly meningitis outbreaks in Africa.

column3: 000 doses of the older polysaccharide vaccine (produced by Instituto Finlay and Bio-Manguinhos)

column6: and 200

column9: C

column1: ### Meningitis vaccines: a problematic supply

column2: which stretches across the continent from Senegal to Ethiopia
column3: affecting 21 countries
column4: is hyperendemic for this disease. Cases frequently recur
column5: with periodic outbreaks during the dry season
column6: which runs from December to June.

column1: Large-scale outbreaks in 1996–1997 caused more than 200
column2: 000 cases
column3: including 20
column4: 000 deaths. The most recent large outbreak occurred in 2009
column5: causing more than 80
column6: 000 cases

column2: the cross border movement has complicated tracking and follow up of contacts

column1: WHO is supporting the national authorities in the response to an outbreak of Ebola virus disease (EVD: formerly known as Ebola haemorrhagic fever). The outbreak is now confirmed to be caused by a strain of ebolavirus with very close homology (98%) to the Zaire ebolavirus. This is the first time the disease has been detected in West Africa.

Cases were first reported from forested areas in south-eastern Guinea. The outbreak has rapidly evolved and several districts and Conakry have reported cases and deaths caused by EVD. A small number of suspected cases and deaths has also been reported from neighbouring countries with all of them having crossed from Guinea. Confirmed cases have been reported from Guinea and Liberia.
* [Latest information on suspected and confirmed cases and deaths](https://www.who.int/entity/csr/don/archive/disease/ebola/en/index.html)

column2: along with genus Marburgvirus and genus Cuevavirus. Genus Ebolavirus comprises five distinct species: Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV): Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV): Reston ebolavirus (RESTV): Sudan ebolavirus (SUDV): and Taï Forest ebolavirus (TAFV). BDBV
column3: EBOV
column4: and SUDV have been associated with large EVD outbreaks in Africa
column5: whereas RESTV and TAFV have not. Samples taken from patients in this outbreak have tested positive for EBOV.

column4: who had been fully immunized for their age as part of ongoing stool sample survey activities. No case of paralytic polio has been reported. In addition to routine acute flaccid paralysis
column5: public health authorities have expanded the surveillance to all age groups and have increased enterovirus surveillance and are screening aseptic meningitis cases for polio.

column2: and a nationwide campaign is planned for 18 August 2013 for children up to the age of nine years. The objective of these SIAs with OPV is to boost mucosal immunity levels in cohorts of children naïve to OPV to rapidly interrupt virus circulation.

Wild poliovirus type 1 (WPV1) has been isolated in 30 sewage samples from 10 sampling sites in Israel. The samples were collected from 3 February 2013 to 30 June 2013. Most positive WPV1 samples were detected from southern Israel. All viruses have been detected in sewage only: no cases of paralytic polio have been reported.

Detection of viruses across the country indicates increased geographic extent of circulation for a prolonged period of time. WHO assesses the risk of further international spread of WPV from Israel as moderate to high.

Health authorities in Israel are continuing to conduct a full epidemiological and public health investigation to actively search for potential cases of paralytic polio and any un-immunized persons. Routine immunization coverage is estimated at 94 percent or above over last eight years. The frequency of environmental surveillance sampling has been increased. Environmental surveillance is frequently used by countries around the world
column2: including in Israel
column3: to support the detection of diseases of public health importance. Similar activities are being implemented by health authorities in Gaza and West Bank and no WPV has been detected to date from these areas.

These SIAs follow efforts initiated beginning of June 2013 to catch-up with any un or under immunized children using inactivated polio vaccine (IPV).

column1: 2011-11-11T00:00:00Z;2011_11_11-en;;;Nigeria: mass lead poisoning from mining activities
column2: Zamfara State - Update 1;;;"*11 November 2011 -*

column1: The mass lead poisoning from mining activities in Zamfara State in Nigeria
column2: which was discovered in March 2010
column3: continues to affect villagers in three Local Government Areas (LGAs): Anka
column4: Bukkuyum and Maru.

column1: While the full scale of the problem is still not fully determined
column2: a survey carried out by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (US CDC) at the request of the Nigeria Federal Ministry of Health has revealed at least 43 villages in Zamfara State where there are confirmed cases of lead poisoning (blood lead concentration >10 μg/dL). In at least seven of these villages there are children who need chelation therapy (blood lead concentration >45 μg/dL). This is in addition to the seven villages that have now been remediated.

column1: With the combined effects of removal from lead exposure and chelation and other supportive therapy
column2: the mortality rate among exposed children in seven remediated villages has dropped from 43% in 2010 to 1% in 2011.

column1: #### Actions taken
WHO and multiple partners have been assisting state and federal authorities to manage the situation
column2: which cannot be resolved without sustained changes to mining practices to prevent further environmental contamination with lead. These include relocation of ore processing activities and storage of ore materials away from villages
column3: the adoption of new processing methods that produce less dust
column4: as well as hygiene measures such as removing contaminated clothes and washing before returning home.

column1: WHO is continuing to advocate with the Government in Nigeria for their attention to this problem and to gain their commitment to further sustained action to prevent the serious and life-long consequences of lead poisoning in a generation of children in Zamfara.
The response to the mass lead poisoning in Zamfara State has involved multiple agencies
column2: including WHO
column3: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
column4: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
column5: United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) - Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) Joint Environment Unit
column6: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
column7: the US CDC
column8: the Blacksmith Institute
column9: TerraGraphics Environmental Engineering Inc
column10: and the Artisanal Gold Council
column11: working with authorities and leaders at community

column1: With funding of US$ 1.9 million provided by the UN Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) to WHO and UNICEF
column2: the following activities have been carried out:

column1: * remediation of five villages (Abare
column2: Tungar Guru
column3: Tungar Daji
column4: Sunke and Duza):

column1: * social mobilization and community awareness activities directed at informing local communities about the hazards of lead and how to prevent lead exposure
column2: including safer mining and gold extraction processes:

column1: * advocacy activities with state and federal authorities
column2: and community leaders:

column1: * establishment of a surveillance system for the early detection of lead poisoning in Zamfara State:
* provision of three hand-held x-ray fluorescence devices for the rapid measurement of lead concentrations in soil:
* provision of four point-of-care analyzers and their kits for the rapid measurement of blood lead concentrations:
* provision of a graphite furnace atomic absorption spectrometer
column2: ancillary equipment and reagents
column3: as well as technical advice
column4: for the establishment of a reference laboratory for the measurement of lead:

column1: * training for doctors
column2: nursing and laboratory staff at the planned lead treatment centre in Gusau on the diagnosis and management of lead poisoning:

column1: * provision of antidotal agents for the treatment of lead poisoning:
* co-ordination of partners involved in the response activities.
The remediation work has been organized by the Blacksmith Institute and TerraGraphics Environmental Engineering Inc
column2: working with the Zamfara State authorities and local contractors. Remediation has involved the identification of contaminated areas in the villages
column3: removal of all contaminated soil
column4: its disposal in secure landfill sites and its replacement with clean soil. In addition walls and other surfaces in family compounds have been cleaned. A total of seven villages have now been remediated
column5: two having been completed before the CERF funding was available. TerraGraphics has provided training in assessment and remediation procedures so that they can be continued by local agencies.

column1: MSF has continued to provide chelation therapy for lead-poisoned children in the decontaminated villages and now has over 2 000 children under five years of age on its treatment programme.
#### Ongoing challenges

This serious environmental emergency cannot be resolved quickly. Remediation is a challenging and time-consuming task. Children have to wait for their family compounds to be cleaned before they can start treatment
column2: and some children will require chelation for many months. Persuading people to adopt new practices and behaviours requires continuing effort. In addition
column3: capacities within Nigeria for the diagnosis and management of lead poisoning need further strengthening and support. A further challenge is the purchase of sufficient chelating agents: these are expensive drugs that are not available as generics. There is therefore a need for long-term engagement on the part of leaders and authorities at community
column4: state and federal levels in Nigeria
column5: as well as health and environment professionals
column6: technical partners and donors.

column1: Of particular concern is the town of Bagega in Anka Local Government Area
column2: which is a regional hub for ore processing and the informal gold trade. Many family compounds and communal areas in the town have soil lead concentrations above 1 000 ppm (400 ppm is the limit in the USA for areas where there are children)
column3: and it is estimated that 1 500 young children may be poisoned with lead. Before these children can be treated they must have a clean environment to live in. There is therefore an urgent need to decontaminate Bagega and the other villages and to provide chelation and other therapy.";;;https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2011_11_11-en

column1: 2011-10-07T00:00:00Z;2011_10_07-en;;;Measles outbreaks: Regions of the Americas
column2: Europe and Africa;;;"7 OCTOBER 2011 - In 2011 several large measles outbreaks have been reported from Member States in the European and African regions
column3: with several reported outbreaks in the Americas linked to Europe or Africa.

column1: **Europe:**  As of 20 September 2011
column2: 40 of 53 Member States in the WHO European Region have reported 26 025 confirmed measles cases for the period January – July 2011 to the WHO European Regional Office through routine surveillance and outbreak reports. The highest number of cases was reported from France with 14 025 cases for the first six months of the year. In addition
column3: eleven of all cases in the Region were lethal (6 in France and one in each of Germany
column4: Kyrgyzstan
column5: Romania
column6: the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and the United Kingdom). The predominant genotype currently circulating in the European Region is D4
column7: the same endemic genotype from the United Kingdom in 2008. The most recent outbreak was reported from Israel in September
column8: with 12 cases. Member States have responded to the outbreak by modifying the vaccination schedule
column9: like France
column10: or by offering vaccination free of charge or in schools
column11: to increase accessibility to and availability of vaccines.

column1: **Africa:** The Regional Office reports that as of September 2011 large measles outbreaks are being reported by the Democratic Republic of the Congo
column2: with over 103 000 cases
column3: Nigeria
column4: with 17 428 cases
column5: and Zambia
column6: with 5 397 cases
column7: and Ethiopia
column8: with 2 902 cases. Even though deaths are not routinely reported to the Regional Office
column9: the WHO Country Office in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports over 1100 measles-associated deaths in the country during 2011.

column1: **Americas:** The last case of endemic measles was reported from the region in 2002. In 2011 the Region has received reports of several outbreaks linked to importation of measles virus from other regions. The largest
column2: in Quebec
column3: Canada
column4: involves 742 reported cases
column5: 89 requiring hospitalization

column7: Ecuador (41 cases)

column9: Columbia (7 cases)

column12: except for outbreaks in the United States and Chile linked to cases from Malaysia and the outbreak in Ecuador

column1: Measles is a highly infectious disease that causes complications and deaths
column2: even in previously-healthy individuals
column3: but is fully preventable by vaccination. Countries need to ensure that they reach 95% coverage with two doses of measles vaccine across all age groups up to 15 years of age. Otherwise the country will experience measles outbreaks with large numbers of cases
column4: associated hospitalizations and deaths. The recent outbreaks in countries with high volumes of international travellers can lead to measles exportation to regions previously free of measles
column5: such as the Region of the Americas or certain African countries. These exportations can lead to large outbreaks and associated deaths.

2011-09-20T00:00:00Z;2011_09_20-en;;;Confirmed international spread of wild poliovirus from Pakistan;;;"*20 September 2011 -*

Wild poliovirus type 1 (WPV1) genetically linked to virus currently circulating in Pakistan has been isolated in [China](http://www.who.int/csr/don/2011_09_01/en/index.html). Pakistan is affected by nationwide transmission of WPV1
column2: and is the location of the only wild poliovirus type 3 (WPV3) case in Asia in 2011 (a strain on the verge of elimination on the continent). As at 13 September 2011
column3: Pakistan had reported 84 cases
column4: compared to 48 cases for the same period in 2010.

column2: supplementary immunization activities (SIAs) in Pakistan have been inadequate in quality in key high-risk areas. In security-compromised parts of the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA)
column3: and in particular in Khyber agency
column4: upwards of 200
column5: 000 children have been regularly missed during SIAs conducted during the last two years. In addition to challenges relating to reaching children in insecure areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and FATA
column6: significant operational challenges continue to mar the quality of SIAs in accessible areas of Khyber and in other key transmission areas of the country
column7: notably in the provinces of Balochistan and Sindh. At the same time
column8: undetected circulation cannot be ruled out due to persistent subnational surveillance gaps. Given these factors
column9: the widespread transmission of WPV1
column10: documented spread internationally
column11: and the detection of the only WPV3 in Asia in 2011
column12: the World Health Organization (WHO) rates as 'high' the risk of further international spread of WPV from Pakistan
column13: particularly given the expected large-scale population movements associated with Umrah and the upcoming Hajj (pilgrimage to Mecca
column14: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia) in the coming months.

column1: To urgently address the widespread transmission of wild poliovirus affecting the country
column2: the Government of Pakistan has this year launched a National Polio Emergency Action Plan
column3: under the auspices His Excellency the President. However
column4: the impact of the Plan is not yet being seen at the critical programme implementation level. To rapidly build up population immunity levels to both serotypes
column5: staggered subnational immunization days are planned for 19-21 September
column6: to be closely followed by further activities in high-risk union councils in 54 districts of the country. However
column7: key to success will be to overcome remaining operational challenges in fully-accessible areas and implemented special outreach strategies with full community participation to increase access to populations in security-compromised areas. To achieve this
column8: full and consistent engagement and accountability at provincial
column9: district and union-council level is urgently needed.

column1: It is important that countries across Asia and the Eastern Mediterranean strengthen disease surveillance for acute flaccid paralysis (AFP)
column2: in order to rapidly detect any poliovirus importations and facilitate a rapid response should importation occur. Countries should also continue to boost routine immunization coverage against all strains of polio to minimize the consequences of any introduction.

column1: As per recommendations outlined in WHO's *International travel and health*
column2: travellers to and from Pakistan should be fully protected by vaccination. Travellers to Pakistan who have in the past received three or more doses of OPV should be offered another dose of polio vaccine before departure. Any unimmunized individuals intending to travel to Pakistan should complete a full course of vaccination. Travellers from Pakistan should have a full course of vaccination against polio before leaving Pakistan
column3: with a minimum one dose of OPV before departure. Some polio-free countries may also require travellers from Pakistan to be immunized against polio in order to obtain an entry visa.

column1: With Hajj and Umrah season already started
column2: the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has issued vaccination requirements for travellers (all ages) for Umrah and Hajj. These requirements are in line with recommendations outlined in WHO's *International travel and health*
column3: with the addition that travellers of all ages from polio endemic countries are required to show proof of vaccination with OPV six weeks before travel to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
column4: and will receive a further dose of OPV upon their arrival.

column1: 2008-07-10T00:00:00Z;2008_07_10-en;;;Case of Marburg Haemorrhagic Fever imported into the Netherlands from Uganda;;;"**10 July 2008**

column2: Germany.

column3: and entered caves on two occasions. The first cave was visited on 16 June at Fort Portal. No bats were seen in this cave. This cave is thought to harbour bat species that have been found to carry filoviruses in other locations in sub-Saharan Africa. Filoviruses cause two types of viral haemorrhagic fever: Marburg and Ebola. A large bat population was seen in the cave and the woman is reported to have had direct contact with one bat.

column1: The woman returned to the Netherlands on 28 June in good health. The first symptoms (fever
column2: chills) occurred on 2 July and she was admitted to hospital on 5 July. Rapid clinical deterioration with liver failure and severe haemorrhaging occurred on 7 July. The patient remains in a critical clinical condition.

column2: as a precaution Dutch authorities have alerted the tour operator to avoid visits to the caves until further information is available.

column1: No citizens of other countries were involved in this trip except for a local tour guide
column2: but the cave in the Maramagambo Forrest is known to be a tourist attraction. No measures were taken with respect to the passengers on the flight from Uganda as the flight occurred four days before the onset of symptoms in the patient.

column1: WHO has informed the Ministry of Health Uganda which will take appropriate steps nationally to investigate these events
column2: and WHO has recommended that the MoH advise all residents and travellers to avoid entering caves with bat populations.

column1: **Advice for travellers**

column3: and how and where SARS coronavirus samples were stored.

column1: WHO and Chinese authorities view with concern the occurrence of laboratory-associated SARS cases. WHO urges all Member States to view this latest outbreak as an opportunity to review the biosafety practices of institutions and laboratories working with SARS coronavirus.

column3: animals and the environment. These specimens
column4: which may contain live SARS coronavirus
column5: are still kept in various laboratories around the world. Some of them are stored in laboratories at an inappropriate containment level. SARS coronavirus has also been propagated in reference and research laboratories

column11: should additional cats become infected with H5N1

column1: prevent smallpox

column1: vaccine. This note aims to clarify these issues.

The vaccine which was used for centuries to vaccinate
against smallpox was not made from smallpox
column2: but from vaccinia virus. Vaccinia is a

column1: different virus from the virus which causes smallpox. However
column2: it is a member of the same

column1: family of viruses to which the smallpox virus belongs. The smallpox virus is also known as
variola virus. Mass vaccinations with smallpox vaccine made from vaccinia virus led to the
eradication of smallpox announced by WHO in 1980. People vaccinated with smallpox vaccine
(vaccinia) develop reactions to it which range from mild and transient to severe
column2: and very

column1: rarely
column2: fatal.

column1: 2) Two countries still keep smallpox virus (variola)
stocks.

column1: laboratories still hold stocks of smallpox virus (variola). These are the WHO
Collaborating Centres in Atlanta
column2: USA and Koltsovo
column3: Russian Federation.

column1: 3) Many countries still hold smallpox vaccine (vaccinia)
stocks.
WHO recommends that countries which still have stocks of
smallpox vaccine (vaccinia) maintain these stocks. This recommendation has been made for
two reasons. Firstly
column2: small amounts of vaccine are still needed to vaccinate laboratory

column1: personnel handling vaccinia virus and other members of this virus family. Some of these
viruses are found in nature and cause illness among animals
column2: and some are used in research

column1: to make new
column2: safer vaccines against a variety of infectious diseases. Secondly
column3: smallpox

column1: vaccine (vaccinia) will also be needed in case of a deliberate or accidental release of
smallpox virus (variola)
column2: which is a very unlikely event but currently of great concern to

column1: some countries.
For further information on this topic
column2: see [the summary of the recent meeting of the WHO

column1: Advisory Committee on Variola Virus Research
column2: published in the Weekly Epidemiological

column1: Record.](http://www.who.int/docstore/wer/pdf/2000/wer7506.pdf)
4) Disposal of biological materials and pharmaceuticals
All biological materials and pharmaceuticals such as
vaccines
column2: drugs and diagnostic specimens should be disposed of safely. Some may require

an expert from the Institut Pasteur has investigated the case in close

column2: Médecins sans Frontièrs

column1: Epicentre (Paris) and UNHCR. The team has ensured the patient is

hospital and village contacts of the confirmed case and visited the
household of the case which is located in Plibo Village Maryland County
Liberia. The man lived there with three other men and two women. The
team found two of the three men were sick with fever and extreme
fatigue which could be signs of Ebola virus infection. Both have been
isolated in their home. The third man is well. Of the two women one
